feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence from iteration 0 (entityR2B): every trial on all three tracks ended off track, with no completions. On the oval, line_loss_events averaged 2.15 and max_error sat at the 0.06 m floor. On the s-bend, line_loss_events was only 0.15, but progress was 0.068. So on the s-bend the robot left the line without losing it. Coverage alone will not fix that track. On the slalom, progress was 0.03 with zero line losses, so steering error, not coverage, is the limit there.

What I had to compensate for in the controller: the sensor weights had to be rescaled to the new spread so the steering gain per metre of offset stays at 25. I did this without changing kp, ki or kd. I kept base_speed at 2.0 because the course needs about 1.5 m/s average. I kept last_direction recovery, which the baseline used without visible failure. If your next geometry changes the spread again, the weights must be rescaled the same way or the steering gain will shift.

What to change depending on the next race: (1) If oval line_loss_events fall but s-bend progress stays near 0.07, the limit is not coverage. Keep the geometry and ask the Integrator for a lower base speed or higher kd before changing the sensors again. (2) If steering_oscillation is high with completion intact, reduce wheel_track to 0.10 or raise mass to 1.0. (3) If the slalom rms_error stays high with few line losses, test a forward sensor lead at y = 0.06.
requested_changes: If the next race shows that line_loss_events fall on the oval but s-bend progress stays near the baseline 0.068, keep this sensor spread and change the geometry only after the Integrator tests base speed or derivative gain. Baseline s-bend evidence: 0.15 line losses, but every trial ended off track at progress 0.068.

If the next race shows high steering_oscillation with completion intact, reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10, or raise mass from 0.8 to 1.0, to lower turn authority or raise yaw inertia. Baseline oscillation was 0.10 on the oval and 0.08 on the s-bend, so check whether the new spread raises it.

If the slalom rms_error stays high with few line losses after this spacing change, move the sensors forward to y = 0.06 while keeping x = -0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06. Baseline slalom evidence: max_error 0.060 and progress 0.033 with zero line losses, which points to steering lead rather than coverage.
